non_election_default_rule: Shares for which no valid election is made ('no election shares') are not automatically deemed cash or stock; instead they receive cash consideration, stock consideration, or a combination of both, depending on the elections made by other 21CF stockholders and the proration/reallocation mechanics needed to hit the $35.7 billion cash cap.

Shares for which no valid election was made by the election deadline are treated as 'non-election' shares and are converted into cash or stock consideration according to the allocation procedures in the merger agreement; generally, non-election shares are allocated the undersubscribed form of consideration first.

Shares for which no valid election is made (or election form not timely received) are deemed 'no election.' If Class A average trading value is within the collar, no-election shares receive cash or stock as necessary to achieve the 60/40 cash-stock split. If Class A average trading value is outside the collar, no-election shares are deemed to have elected whichever form of consideration has the higher value, subject to proration/reallocation to achieve the 60/40 split.

Broadcom common shares for which no valid election form was received by the exchange agent by the election deadline are deemed 'cash electing shares' and receive $54.50 cash per share, subject to proration.
Shares with no election, an untimely election, or an ineffective form of election (or a validly revoked election without a new valid submission) are deemed to have made a stock election.

Shares for which no election (or an invalid/untimely election) is made are deemed to be 'share electing shares' and receive the share consideration, subject to the same proration procedures as shares that affirmatively elected stock.

Shares for which no valid election was made ('No Election Shares') were deemed non-electing and had no control over consideration type; treatment depended on which consideration type was oversubscribed/undersubscribed (in the actual event, No Election Shares were treated as Cash Election Shares since stock was oversubscribed).

TopBuild shares for which no valid cash or stock election has been affirmatively made and not revoked by the election deadline ('No Election Shares') are deemed to have elected the Stock Consideration (20.200 QXO shares per share), subject to proration.

Holders who fail to make an election, make an untimely election, or submit an invalid election ('non-electing holders') are deemed to have elected the form of consideration (or mix thereof) remaining after satisfaction of the elections of other holders of common shares. In the cash-oversubscription proration scenario, all BIPC share election shares AND non-election shares are converted into the right to receive the per-share BIPC share consideration.

Shares for which no valid election is made by the election deadline become 'non-election shares' and are allocated to whichever form of consideration (cash or stock) is undersubscribed, before oversubscribed electing shares are prorated into that undersubscribed form. Non-electing holders may receive all cash, all stock, or a mix, depending on remaining pools.

NYSE Euronext stockholders who do not make a valid, timely election (or whose election form is not properly received by the election deadline) are deemed to have elected the Standard Election Amount (0.1703 ICE Group shares + $11.27 cash per share).

Shares for which no valid cash election is made (non-electing shares) are deemed to have made a 'non-election' and, subject to proration, are converted into the right to receive 0.6432 shares of PepsiCo common stock (i.e., default is stock, subject to proration that could convert a portion to cash to true-up the 50/50 split). Shares as to which appraisal rights are not perfected are deemed to have made a cash election.
Shares for which no valid election is made ('non-electing shares') are converted into the right to receive the stock consideration.

Shares for which no valid election was made (non-electing shares) are treated as non-election shares and may be paid all in cash, all in BBVA shares, or part cash and part BBVA shares, depending on the remaining pool of BBVA shares and cash available after honoring valid cash and stock elections made by other stockholders, without regard to the non-electing holder's preference.

Shares for which no valid election form was received by the election deadline ("no election shares") are deemed to have made an equity (common unit) election, subject to proration if equity elections exceed 50% cap.

Shares for which no valid cash election is made (i.e., non-electing shares) receive the stock consideration (Lennar Class A and Class B common stock) in full, not cash. Separately, MP CA Homes LLC (major CalAtlantic stockholder) agreed to be deemed to elect cash for the number of shares necessary to reach the maximum cash amount if other stockholders did not elect enough cash.

Shares for which no valid/timely election form is received are deemed non-election shares. If the 10-trading-day average VWAP of Ecolab common stock ending on the last full trading day before the effective time (the 'Closing Ecolab Stock Price') is greater than $55.39/share, non-election shares are deemed to have elected stock; if less than $55.39, deemed to have elected cash; if exactly $55.39, deemed to receive a mix of stock and cash as necessary to achieve the overall 70%/30% mix. Deemed-election shares are not subject to the same adjustment/reallocation provisions as affirmatively elected shares.
Any Terminix share not covered by a validly submitted election form (including a missed deadline or invalid election) is deemed to have made a Stock Election.

Shares for which no valid election was made (or an improperly completed/unsigned election form, or election not received by deadline) are deemed 'no election shares' and treated as cash election shares (i.e., default to cash), subject to proration.

Shares for which no valid election is made (or election not timely received) are deemed to have elected 'mixed consideration' ($17.10 cash + 0.4543 Invitrogen shares per share), i.e., treated as non-electing shares converted into mixed consideration.

Shares for which no valid election is made by the election deadline are treated as 'non-election shares' and receive merger consideration in whatever form or mix (cash, stock, or a combination) remains after giving effect to the preferences of stockholders who did make elections, at a value approximately equivalent to that received by electing holders.

If a holder does not submit a properly completed and signed election form by the election deadline, or submits a form indicating no election, that holder's shares are converted into the cash consideration ($60.00/share); non-electing shares are not eligible for the unit consideration.

Holders who made no election, an untimely election, or were otherwise deemed not to have submitted an effective form of election (including after revocation without a new valid election) were deemed to have elected stock consideration.

Shares for which no valid election was made by the election deadline were deemed to have elected all-stock consideration (1.61 CCI shares per GSL share); such shares were not counted toward the cash cap/proration pool.

MTGE stockholders who tender/validly hold shares but do not make a valid election (or hold shares as nominees without instructions) will be deemed to have elected, and will receive, the Mixed Consideration ($9.82 cash + 0.9519 Annaly shares per share), subject to proration mechanics.

Shares with no valid election are 'no election shares' and are allocated to the undersubscribed form of consideration first, before electing shares of the oversubscribed form are switched; electing shares have priority over non-election shares in proration.

Common units for which no valid election was made (non-election units) receive such merger consideration as determined in accordance with the proration provisions of the merger agreement (i.e., allocated among share/cash/mixed consideration per proration formula, not a fixed default of pure cash or pure stock).

Shares for which no valid election is made (non-election shares) are converted to the undersubscribed form of consideration first (cash or stock, whichever is undersubscribed), before electing shares of the oversubscribed form are switched pursuant to proration. Non-election shares generally receive lower priority than validly electing shares in proration scenarios.
Shares with no valid election, revoked elections without new election, or election expressing no preference are deemed to have elected the common share (stock) consideration.

Shares with no valid stock election ('No Election Shares') are converted into the right to receive the Cash Consideration ($35.00/share); in no event does a non-electing holder receive stock consideration.

If a holder does not make a valid election (or submits an election form indicating no election) by the election deadline: (i) if the number of shares electing cash exceeds the maximum cash consideration shares, the non-electing holder is deemed to have made a stock election; (ii) if the number of shares electing stock exceeds the maximum stock consideration shares, the non-electing holder is deemed to have made a cash election.
Shares for which no valid election was made ('non-election shares') were converted into the right to receive the cash consideration ($24.00 per share).

Shares as to which the holder has not made a valid election by the election deadline (including revoked elections) are deemed 'non-electing shares' and are allocated cash and/or stock consistent with the proration procedures based on other shareholders' elections (i.e., non-electing shareholders bear the residual allocation risk and typically receive whichever consideration type has the lower value at the time).

Shares for which no valid election is made (or election is revoked and not resubmitted) prior to the election deadline are treated as 'no election shares' and receive the mixed consideration (0.6840 CECO shares + $10.00 cash per share), which is not subject to proration.

Shares for which no valid cash election is made are deemed 'non-election' shares and default to receiving PepsiCo stock (0.5022 shares per PAS share), subject to proration. Shares as to which appraisal rights are lost/withdrawn are deemed to have made a cash election.

Shares for which a Mariner stockholder fails to make a valid election (or election form not received by deadline / improperly completed) are treated as 'non-election shares' and receive the Mixed Consideration: $7.80 cash + 0.17043 Apache shares per share, not subject to proration.

Non-electing shares receive cash if stock elections exceed 70% cap; receive stock if cash elections exceed 50% cap; if neither cap is exceeded, non-electing shares first fill the cash bucket up to 50% of outstanding shares, then remaining non-electing shares receive stock.

Shares for which no valid election is made become 'non-election shares' and are converted to the undersubscribed form of merger consideration (cash or stock) first, ahead of prorating electing shares of the oversubscribed form.

AM unitholders (public) who do not make a valid election by the election deadline are deemed non-electing holders and are deemed to have elected the Public Mixed Consideration ($3.415 cash + 1.6350 shares of New AM common stock per unit).

Holders failing to make a valid election ('no election shares') receive the residual mix of cash and share consideration remaining after giving effect to proration preferences of electing holders (in proportion to respective total cash available and total share elections available, reduced by the acceptance fraction).
Shares for which no valid election is made (or an untimely/ineffective election) are deemed to have elected mixed election consideration ($15.60 cash + 0.2218 shares, subject to proration).

Shares for which no valid election form is received by the election deadline become 'No Election Shares.' No Election Shares are treated per the proration formula: if cash oversubscribed, they receive stock consideration; if cash undersubscribed, some No Election Shares may be selected pro rata to receive cash ('Cash Designated Shares'); otherwise they receive stock. Dissenting shares that lose appraisal rights are also treated as non-electing/no election shares.

FGL shareholders who do not make a valid election (no election submitted, late, improperly completed, unsigned, or revoked without new election) are deemed 'non-electing shares' and will receive cash consideration, stock consideration, or a combination of both, subject to the allocation and proration provisions of the merger agreement (i.e., allocated to balance the cash pool up to the cap).

LIN common shares for which no valid election was made ('no election shares') are converted to the undersubscribed form of consideration first (cash or stock), and only receive a mix of cash/stock if the undersubscribed pool is insufficient to absorb the full no-election share count.
Shares for which no valid election is made ('non-electing shares') are converted into the right to receive Ventas common stock (0.1688 shares) per HCT share, per merger agreement procedures.

Gemstar shares as to which the holder has not made a valid election prior to the election deadline (including due to revocation) are deemed 'non-electing shares.' Non-electing stockholders have no control over the type of consideration received; their shares may be exchanged for cash, stock, or a combination consistent with the proration procedures, and non-electing holders are likely to receive the consideration type having the lower value at the time (since other stockholders would preferentially elect the higher-value option).

Any Conversant stockholder who fails to submit a proper Form of Election by the election deadline (5:00 p.m. NYC time, December 8, 2014) is deemed to have elected to receive the Base Consideration (0.07037 Alliance Data shares + formulaic cash, subject to $14.98-$18.62 cash collar) for each eligible share.
Shares with no valid/timely election (or non-received election form) are deemed to have made the Standard Election Consideration ($16.625 cash + 0.2440 Endo shares per share).
EPL stockholders who do not submit a valid election by the deadline are deemed to have made a Mixed Election ($25.35 cash + 0.584 EXXI shares per EPL share).
Shares for which no valid election is made (including untimely, deficient, or revoked-without-replacement elections) are deemed to have elected the Cash Consideration ($6.65/share).

Shares for which no valid election is made by the election deadline (and for which appraisal has not been properly demanded) are deemed 'No Election Shares' and are treated as having made the Mixed (Standard Mix) Election — i.e., they receive the Standard Mix of Consideration ($40.125 cash + 0.7253 ETP units/share), not subject to proration.

Shares for which no valid election is made become 'non-election' shares and are converted into cash or stock consideration according to allocation procedures in the merger agreement; generally allocated to whichever form is undersubscribed.

SilverBow stockholders who did not submit a valid election form by the election deadline were deemed to have made no election and received the Stock Election Consideration (3.125 Crescent Class A shares per SilverBow share). Shares transferred during the election period were also deemed to elect only Stock Election Consideration unless a subsequent valid election was made.

If a shareholder does not return a valid form of election by the election deadline (or improperly completes it), the shareholder has no control over consideration type; the shares are exchanged for cash or stock consistent with the proration procedures in the merger agreement (may be treated as no-election shares subject to allocation, potentially receiving cash if cash consideration undersubscribed).

Aris securityholders who fail to deliver a valid election (or revoke without a subsequent valid election), and have not demanded appraisal, are deemed to have elected the Common Unit Election Consideration (0.625 WES common units) and are not eligible for the Mixed or Cash Election Consideration.

Shares with no valid election ('no election shares') are treated as available for whichever form of consideration (cash or stock) is undersubscribed; holder has no control over which form is received; realized outcome showed no-election shares received cash consideration.

Shares for which no valid election is made by the deadline become 'non-electing company shares' and are treated as if a Mixed Election had been made, receiving $12.75 cash plus a fraction of a Tyco share equal to $29.75/VWAP (subject to collar).

Chittenden stockholders who failed to submit a properly completed election form (with stock certificates or guaranteed delivery) by the election deadline were deemed non-electing holders. Non-electing holders received merger consideration equivalent in value per share to that paid to electing holders, but the form (cash, stock, or mix) depended on the remaining pool of cash/stock after honoring other stockholders' elections, without regard to the non-electing holder's preference.

Shares for which no valid election was made (or a valid election was revoked/invalid) by the election deadline are deemed 'non-election shares' and are converted into cash or stock consideration according to the proration procedures in the merger agreement. In practice (per realized results), non-election shares received only the stock consideration.

Hatteras stockholders who validly tender but do not make a valid election receive the Mixed Consideration ($5.55 cash + 0.9894 Annaly shares per share). Non-tendering stockholders (post-offer, in the merger) who do not make an election are also deemed to have elected Mixed Consideration.
Holders who fail to make a valid and timely election are deemed to have made the Stock Election (12.7793 WMIH shares per Nationstar share, subject to proration).

Shares/warrants for which no valid election was made ('No Election Shares') are deemed not to have elected cash or stock. If either the cash election or stock election is oversubscribed (i.e., exceeds its respective cap), No Election Shares are deemed to have elected the oversubscribed consideration type; if neither is oversubscribed, No Election Shares are deemed to have elected the consideration type selected by the majority of shares/warrants for which a valid election was made.

Shares for which no valid election is made ("no election shares") are used first to fill any shortfall toward the total cash number (i.e., converted to cash pro rata among no-election shares) if cash is undersubscribed. If cash is oversubscribed, no-election holders receive stock consideration. Absent a proper election form by the deadline, holder is deemed to have expressed no preference and may receive cash, stock, or a combination of both depending on other stockholders' elections.

Shares with no valid election ('non-election shares') are allocated stock or cash consideration based on the proration procedures/remaining pool after elections; non-electing holders receive consideration valued at $80.00 but may receive all cash, all stock, or a mix depending on other stockholders' elections.

Resolute common shares for which no valid election was made (non-election shares) are deemed to receive the Mixed Election Consideration ($14.00 cash + 0.2366 Cimarex shares per share), subject to proration.

Shares for which no valid election was made ('non-election shares') were converted into stock or cash consideration according to the allocation/proration procedures (i.e., subject to the same 86/14 proration as electing shares), not a fixed default to cash or stock.

Non-election shares (no valid election made, or shares tendered without an effective election form) are allocated according to the proration/allocation procedures after all valid elections are processed: if cash oversubscribed, non-election shares go to stock consideration; if stock oversubscribed, non-election shares go to cash consideration; if neither cap exceeded, non-election shares are converted pro rata first into stock (until stock reaches 45% of tendered shares) with any remainder into cash.

AGA stockholders who tendered shares without making a valid cash or stock election were treated as making 'no election.' If 50%+ of tendered shares validly elected cash, non-electing holders were deemed to have elected stock (and vice versa if stock was oversubscribed). If neither form was oversubscribed, non-electing holders received a pro rata mix such that overall 50% cash / 50% stock was achieved across all tendered shares.

Shares for which no valid election is made by the deadline are designated 'non-election shares.' Holders of non-election shares have no control over consideration type and may receive only cash, only stock, or a mix of cash and stock, determined by the proration adjustment based on other shareholders' elections.
Non-electing (or invalid/untimely electing) WildHorse holders are deemed to have elected the Share Consideration (5.989 Chesapeake shares per WildHorse share, no cash).

Shares for which no valid election is made (or election is revoked without replacement, or 'No Election' box checked) are designated 'non-election shares'/holder becomes 'non-electing stockholder.' These shares/holders have no control over consideration type; they receive stock or cash (or a mix) based on the proration/allocation procedures depending on whether the stock election was oversubscribed or undersubscribed - could receive all stock, all cash, or a mix.

Holders who fail to make a valid election, or who revoke an election without submitting a new one, are deemed 'non-electing holders' and are treated as having made the Share & CVR Election (0.743 TPRE share + 1 CVR per Sirius share).

Shares for which no valid election is made (non-election shares) are allocated stock consideration or cash consideration by the exchange agent depending on the elections made by other shareholders under the proration/allocation procedures (i.e., non-election shares are treated as part of the pool used to balance the 70%/30% stock/cash split, prioritized ahead of stock-election shares in cash-undersubscribed scenarios).

Shares for which no valid election is made (election form not returned/not timely completed, or holder indicates no preference) are 'no-election shares' subject to allocation under Section 3.3 (could receive cash or stock depending on proration outcome). Dissenting shares that lose appraisal rights after the election deadline are treated as non-election shares; dissenting shares generally are deemed cash election shares.

Shares for which no valid election was made (including failure to submit a properly completed election form by the deadline) are deemed non-election shares and receive the stock consideration (1.85 BridgeBio shares per Eidos share).

Shares for which no valid election is made by the election deadline are treated as 'non-election shares' and are converted into the right to receive the per share stock consideration or per share cash consideration according to the allocation/proration procedures; generally, non-election shares are allocated to whichever form of consideration (cash or stock) is undersubscribed, and are the first shares redesignated when reallocating to meet the cash cap.

Non-electing shares (no valid election submitted by deadline) receive: if stock elections >80% of non-dissenting shares, non-electors get $19.06 cash; if cash elections >20% of non-dissenting shares, non-electors get 0.19409 Equinix shares; if within both thresholds, non-electors may receive either stock or cash (or a mix), determined by the exchange agent by lot or another reasonable method selected by Equinix.

Shareholders who fail to make a valid, timely election (or whose election forms are improperly completed/unsigned or received after the deadline) are deemed non-electing holders. Non-electing holders receive merger consideration equivalent in value to that paid to electing holders, but the form of consideration (all cash, all stock, or part cash/part stock) depends on the remaining pool of cash and stock available after honoring other shareholders' valid cash and stock elections, subject to proration for cash if the minimum stock percentage is not met. Non-electing holders' preferences are not considered in the allocation. If the minimum stock percentage is not met, non-electing shares are converted to stock consideration (in the stock-cap-exceeded scenario, converted to cash).

Shares of holders who indicate no preference or fail to make a valid election are deemed 'non-election' (no-election) shares. No-election shares receive the per-share stock consideration unless there is an oversubscription of the stock consideration, in which case they may receive the per-share cash consideration for some or all of their shares.

Shares for which a holder does not make a valid election (or revokes without timely submitting a new election) are deemed to have made a 'non-election,' and non-electing shares are deemed to have made the mixed cash/stock election (1.137 shares of DigitalGlobe common stock + $4.10 cash per share).

Shares for which no valid election is made (or election form/certificates not properly submitted by the deadline) are treated as non-election shares; holders may be paid all cash, all Seawell stock, or a mix of cash and stock depending on the elections made by other stockholders (i.e., non-election shares absorb the residual consideration mix after cash/stock elections and proration are applied).
Shares with no election, untimely election, invalid election, or unrevoked prior election are deemed to have made a Mixed Election ($12.64 cash + 0.4034 shares, subject to proration).

Non-electing tendered shares receive whatever consideration form remains after all valid elections are satisfied (or pro rata share of each if neither is oversubscribed). If cash elections >= 55% of tendered shares (oversubscribed), non-electing shares are treated as stock elections. If stock elections >= 45% of tendered shares (oversubscribed), non-electing shares are treated as cash elections. If neither is oversubscribed, non-electing shares receive a pro rata mix such that overall 55%/45% cash/stock split is maintained.

Shares tendered without a valid election (or not tendered but converted in back-end merger without election) are deemed to have elected, and will receive, the Mixed Consideration ($5.04 cash + 0.6549 Cott shares per share, subject to the same aggregate proration).

Shares for which no valid election is made ('non-election shares') are allocated per proration rules: generally, non-election shares are allocated first to whichever form of consideration (cash or stock) is undersubscribed, before any oversubscribed-electing shares are switched; non-election shares have lower priority than validly and timely made elections.

Shares for which no valid election is made become 'non-election shares' and are allocated to whichever form of consideration (cash or stock) is undersubscribed, ahead of electing shareholders of the oversubscribed form, per proration procedures in the merger agreement.
Pope units for which a valid election is not timely received by the election deadline are deemed to have made the Stock Election Consideration (3.929 Rayonier shares per unit), subject to proration.

Shareholders who make no election or an invalid election are deemed 'non-election shares.' Non-election shares are allocated stock or cash consideration per the proration formula (Section 2.3(b)): they are treated similarly to a buffer used to fill any shortfall between stock elections and the stock conversion number before cash election shares are affected. Holders with non-election shares have no control over what type of consideration (cash, stock, or mix) they receive.
Cornell stockholders who fail to make a valid election (non-election shares) will receive the stock consideration (1.3 GEO shares per Cornell share); non-election shares are not pro-rated into cash.
Shares for which no valid election is made (no-election shares) are treated as having elected stock consideration and will receive ERI common stock (not subject to being selected into the cash pool).

Shares for which no valid election is made by the election deadline (non-election shares) are deemed to have made a Mixed Election and receive the Mixed Consideration (0.6522 Cincinnati Bell shares + $18.45 cash per share), not subject to proration.

Under the August 2008 form of election, shares for which no valid election is made are deemed 'No Election' and receive only stock consideration (0.8 Heckmann shares per China Water share). Under the earlier July 2008 form of election and letter of transmittal, no-election shares were deemed to have 'no preference' and would receive merger consideration based on the allocation/proration procedures set forth in the merger agreement (not automatically all-stock).

Shareholders who do not make a valid election (non-electing) will have no control over the type of consideration received; their shares will be allocated cash, stock, or a mix based on the proration procedures and the elections made by other shareholders. Because other shareholders tend to elect based on relative values, non-electing shareholders are likely to receive the form of consideration with the lower relative value at the effective time.

Shares for which no valid election is made (non-election/no preference shares) are allocated cash, M&T stock, or a combination thereof based on the remaining pool of cash and stock available after honoring valid cash and stock elections, per the allocation/proration procedures; non-electing holders receive equivalent value ($12.50/share) but consideration mix depends on other stockholders' elections.
Shares for which no valid election is made (or an invalid/untimely election form is submitted) are deemed not to have made an election and default to receiving 100% cash consideration.

Shares for which no valid election is made by the election deadline are deemed non-electing shares and are treated as if the holder elected the share consideration (i.e., converted into ANGI Homeservices Class A common stock).
S1 stockholders who do not make a valid election are deemed to have elected the cash consideration (non-election shares treated as cash election shares, subject to proration).

MSLO stockholders who do not make a valid election (non-electing holders) receive, for each share, either $6.15 cash or the same number of Holdings shares as if they had made a stock election, subject to proration; treated as 'non-election shares' for purposes of proration formula (Scenario 1/2 rules based on shortfall vs. non-election share count).

Shares with no valid election, improperly completed elections, or elections not timely received are deemed 'non-election shares.' These shares are allocated cash or stock (or a mix) depending on the proration outcome of other shareholders' elections — non-election shares are treated as cash-first in the base case (if Stock Election Number is within Min/Max range) but may receive stock if there's a shortfall in the stock election pool.

Shares with no valid election are treated as 'no election' shares; in the actual (cash-oversubscribed) scenario they received the stock consideration (1.6839 Bioventus shares); had cash been undersubscribed, no-election shares would have received priority cash allocation before stock-election shares.

Shares as to which a holder made a valid 'no preference' election, or as to which no valid election was made (including due to revocation), are deemed 'non-election shares.' Depending on whether cash elections exceed or fall short of the fixed cash conversion number, non-election/no-preference shares will receive stock consideration (if cash oversubscribed) or may receive cash consideration despite no cash election (if cash undersubscribed).

Shares for which no valid election is made become 'non-election shares' and are allocated to whichever form of consideration (cash or stock) is undersubscribed, before oversubscribed-electing shares are reallocated to that undersubscribed form.

Anchor stockholders who did not submit a valid, timely election form were deemed 'non-election' shares. Non-election shares are allocated first to whichever form of consideration (cash or stock) is undersubscribed, before shares of stockholders who affirmatively elected the oversubscribed form are switched/prorated. Thus, electing shareholders have priority over non-election shares when proration is necessary.

Shares for which no valid election is made (or election is revoked without a new valid election) are treated as 'no election shares.' No-election shares are used first to fill any shortfall toward the cash election threshold (before stock election shares are reallocated), but in the proration/allocation process, no-election shares are deprioritized relative to shares for which a timely election was properly made when oversubscription occurs (i.e., they generally get the undersubscribed form of consideration before oversubscribed-electing shares are switched).
Shares tendered without a valid election are deemed to have made a stock election (subject to proration and cash-in-lieu of fractional shares).

Shares for which no valid election is made by the election deadline ('non-election shares') are converted into the cash consideration or the stock consideration according to the proration procedures set forth in the merger agreement (generally allocated first to the undersubscribed form of consideration).

Shares for which no valid election is made (non-election) are not automatically cash or stock; instead they receive consideration based on the results of the proration procedures, filling whatever allocation (cash or stock) remains after processing valid elections. Because other shareholders' elections are taken into account, non-electing holders are likely to receive the form of consideration having the lower value.

Shares of holders who indicate no preference or fail to make a valid election ('non-election shares') default to the per-share stock consideration, unless there is an oversubscription of the stock consideration pool, in which case some or all of such shares may instead receive the per-share cash consideration.
Merchants stockholders who fail to make a timely/valid election, or make no election, receive the mixed election consideration (0.6741 CBU shares + $12.00 cash per share).

Shares for which no valid election is made (or election form not properly submitted/received by deadline) are treated as 'no-election shares' and are subject to allocation/proration along with cash- and stock-election shares to achieve the 45% cash/55% stock aggregate split; no-election shareholders may not receive the same form of consideration as if they had elected.

Shares for which no valid election is made (non-election) receive no guaranteed consideration type; treatment depends on whether the stock election is oversubscribed or undersubscribed. In the oversubscription example given, non-election shares (along with cash-election shares) are converted entirely into cash consideration. The undersubscription example in the same filing assumes no non-election shares.

Stockholders who fail to submit a valid, timely election (or submit an improperly completed/unsigned election form) are deemed non-electing 'non-election shares' and receive the mixed cash-and-stock consideration ($1.73 cash + stock valued at $1.27 via exchange ratio), same as mixed electors, subject to proration.

Shares as to which no valid election is made (non-election shares) will receive the stock consideration and/or cash consideration as determined pursuant to the allocation provisions of the merger agreement without regard to preference. Specifically, non-electing shareholders will be treated as though they elected all cash, unless cash has been fully subscribed by electing shareholders, in which case they will be treated as if they elected all stock.

Shareholders who did not make a valid election (or whose forms were not timely/properly completed) had no control over the consideration received; per the S-4, non-election shares would receive merger consideration based on the allocation/proration procedures. Per the actual completion 8-K, non-electing shareholders ultimately received only stock consideration (because stock was undersubscribed relative to the 60% target in the actual results).

Shares for which no valid election is made (non-election/no-election shares) are allocated cash and/or stock based on the elections of other shareholders and the allocation/proration procedures; non-electing shareholders are subordinate in priority to electing shareholders when re-allocation is needed. Per the December 2011 results release, non-electing shares were ultimately treated as receiving stock consideration (4.686 shares per share).

Shares for which no valid election is made are 'non-election shares.' They receive a mix of cash and stock consideration depending on the aggregate elections of other stockholders (used to fill any shortfall in the 60%/40% target before pro rata reallocation of electing shareholders' consideration).

Shares for which no valid election is made (non-election shares) are deemed non-election shares and are allocated per the proration formula: if stock election number is within min/max range, non-election shares receive cash consideration; if stock election number is below minimum (shortfall), non-election shares are first used to fill the stock shortfall (converted to stock consideration) up to the shortfall amount, with any remainder receiving cash.

Shares for which no valid election is made ('no election'/non-election shares) are used first to satisfy any shortfall needed to reach the 50% stock floor (converted to stock/cash mix); if the shortfall exceeds non-election shares, all non-election shares are converted to stock. If the stock election number is between 50%-65%, non-election shares receive cash or stock at United's discretion. If stock elections exceed 65%, non-election shares are deemed cash elections.

Shareholders who did not make a timely or valid election were deemed to have made 'no election'; such non-election shares were used first in the allocation/proration process to balance the mandated 90% stock / 10% cash split. In the final results, all non-election shares were allocated all-stock consideration because cash elections alone exceeded the 10% cash pool.

Shares for which no valid cash or stock election was made (non-election shares), or for which the election form was not timely/properly submitted, are automatically converted into the right to receive cash consideration only ($6.50/share), not subject to proration.

Shares for which no valid election is made (or where broker fails to instruct) are treated as 'no-election shares' and are subject to the allocation procedures — i.e., they are allocated cash and/or stock depending on the elections made by other shareholders and the average WaFd share price, to fill whatever shortfall remains after honoring cash/stock elections, subject to the overall 50/50 split requirement. In an oversubscription-of-cash scenario, no-election shares are converted entirely to WaFd stock.

Non-election shares are treated as follows: if stock is oversubscribed, non-election shares receive cash; if stock is undersubscribed and non-election shares are sufficient to cover the shortfall, non-election shareholders receive a mix of cash and stock to make up the shortfall (cash electors get cash); if non-election shares are insufficient to cover the shortfall, non-election shareholders receive all stock and cash electors receive a mix of cash/stock.

Non-electing (or invalid-election) IBT shareholders will receive merger consideration equal in value to that paid to electing holders, but may be paid all cash, all stock, or a mix, depending on the remaining pool of cash and stock available after honoring valid cash and stock elections; per the post-election press release, shares with no election were converted into cash consideration at $31.00 per share.

Shares with no valid election submitted by the deadline are treated as 'non-electing' shares. UCBH first uses these non-electing shares as a buffer to satisfy shareholders who did make elections (allocating them to cash or stock as needed to preserve others' specific elections and to reach the mandated 50%/50% cash/stock split). If there are insufficient non-electing shares to absorb an oversubscription, specific elections themselves are prorated instead.

Shares for which no valid election is made ('non-electing shares') are converted into a combination of cash and Midland stock, determined by dividing any excess available cash (after mixed-election shares) by the number of non-electing shares, plus 0.65x the exchange ratio in stock (i.e., non-electing shares are treated similarly to mixed-consideration electing shares based on residual availability).

Any common unit for which a properly completed election form and letter of transmittal is not submitted by the election deadline, or with respect to which no election is made, is deemed to have elected to receive the cash merger consideration ($1.55/unit).

Vision shareholders who do not make a valid election (non-electing shares) will be deemed to have elected the form of merger consideration (cash or Park stock) for which less than 50% of total Vision shares have elected — i.e., they are allocated to the undersubscribed consideration type.

If a holder does not make an election by the deadline (4:00 p.m. local time on September 18, 2017), First Bancorp has the authority to determine the type of consideration (cash, stock, or mix) for such non-election shares.

Shareholders who do not make a timely, valid election are deemed to have elected to receive the mixed consideration of cash and stock (no-election shares are prorated as needed to achieve the 70%/30% stock/cash split).

Shares for which no valid election was made (non-election shares) are allocated to cash or stock based on the shortfall/oversubscription mechanics described in the merger agreement — i.e., non-electing shares fill any shortfall in the cash or stock pools on a pro rata basis; if cash election shares are less than the cash conversion number, non-election shares (along with stock election shares) are allocated pro rata to cash to make up the shortfall.

Shares without a valid election (or with no-election box checked) are deemed to have made the Cash Election, entitling holder to up to $7.30 cash per share (balance paid in Atheros stock, subject to proration).

Shares for which no valid election is made (non-election) are not entitled to a fixed form of consideration; they receive cash, stock, or a combination depending on the proration results and elections of other shareholders. Per the August 26, 2013 press release, non-electing shares (and stock electors) received all-stock consideration because cash was oversubscribed.

Stockholders who do not submit a properly completed election form (or who revoke it) prior to the election deadline are designated 'non-election shares.' Per the oversubscription provision, non-election shares are allocated to whichever consideration type (cash or stock) is undersubscribed relative to the 50/50 target.

Shares whose holders do not make a valid election (fail to submit a properly completed election form and certificates by the deadline, select 'no election', or revoke without resubmitting) are deemed 'non-election shares' and are convertible, at S&T's discretion, into cash, stock, or a combination thereof, subject to the allocation/proration provisions of the merger agreement.

If a holder does not make a timely valid election, the shares are treated as though the holder elected to receive all stock, unless the stock option has been fully subscribed by electing HPTB shareholders, in which case the non-electing shares are treated as though the holder elected all cash.

PMFG stockholders who fail to make a valid election by the election deadline are deemed to have made a non-election; they have no control over the form of consideration received. The consideration received by non-electing holders depends on which form of merger consideration (cash or stock) is oversubscribed or undersubscribed at the election deadline.

If cash elections exceed the cash cap, non-electing shares receive stock; if stock elections exceed the stock cap, non-electing shares receive cash; otherwise (no proration triggered), non-electing shares receive a pro rata mix of remaining cash and stock consideration after allocations to electing holders.

Shares with no valid election become 'non-election shares' and are converted into cash, stock, or a combination as needed to satisfy the aggregate cash and aggregate stock consideration requirements per the proration methodology (i.e., allocated to whichever side needs filling to meet the caps).

Holders who fail to submit a valid, timely election form are deemed to have elected the combination option: cash for 40% of their shares and Renasant stock for the remaining 60% of their shares, at the same price/exchange ratio.

Shares for which no valid election is made before the election deadline are converted into the right to receive CBU common stock (at the 0.5635 ratio), $20.00 cash, or a combination of both, as determined by CBU pursuant to the same allocation/proration procedures applied to all shares (not a fixed pre-set 'mixed' default).

Shares with no valid/timely election ('no-election shares') are allocated cash and/or Harleysville stock in amounts necessary to satisfy the aggregate cash and stock consideration allocation requirements under the merger agreement (i.e., no-election shares absorb whatever consideration type is needed to balance the aggregate cap). At closing, remaining no-election/cash-election shareholders received $14.50 cash per share.

Non-election shares (shares for which no election, or an untimely/incomplete election, was made) are allocated according to the proration/allocation mechanism depending on whether stock or cash consideration is oversubscribed - they are not automatically deemed cash or stock but are subject to the same 50/50 balancing mechanism, generally absorbed into whichever pool is needed to restore the 50/50 split (e.g., in a stock oversubscription scenario, non-election shares are converted to cash consideration).

Shares for which no valid election is made (or delivery of certificates fails) are deemed 'non-election shares' and are converted into cash and/or stock consideration according to the proration procedures — i.e., they receive whichever form of consideration is undersubscribed, or a mix if neither election is oversubscribed.

Shares for which no valid election is made (or election revoked) are designated 'non-election shares' and are allocated cash or stock consistent with overall proration mechanics; per final election results release, non-electing shareholders received 0.9218 shares of Investors stock per share.

Shares for which a holder does not submit a properly completed election form (or revokes without resubmitting) by the election deadline are designated 'no-election shares.' These are allocated per the proration formula: first deemed cash election shares (pro rata) to the extent needed to fill the 40% cash cap; any remainder is treated as common stock election shares.

Shares for which no election is made (or an election form is not properly completed/timely returned) are 'non-election shares'; the consideration a non-electing stockholder receives depends on the elections made by other Peoples stockholders and the proration/allocation procedures used to achieve the 60% stock/40% cash split (non-election shares are allocated to whichever pool — cash or stock — is undersubscribed after cash/stock electing shares are processed).

Shares for which no valid election was made by the election deadline are deemed 'non-election shares' and are converted to cash and/or stock per the proration formula (Section 3.2.6), not automatically all-cash or all-stock. Dissenting shares are deemed cash-election shares.

Shares with no valid election are 'non-election shares' and are allocated cash or stock (or a combination) depending on the proration needed to reach the 50% stock / 50% cash target — non-election holders are treated similarly to cash electors in oversubscription scenarios (receive cash if stock oversubscribed) but may receive stock to fill shortfall if stock undersubscribed and shortfall <= non-election shares.

Shareholders who do not submit a properly completed and signed form of election by the election deadline (non-election or invalid election) will have no control over the type of consideration received; if the cash election is oversubscribed, non-electing/invalid-electing holders receive stock consideration (subject to proration).

Shares for which no valid election is made ('non-election shares') are allocated cash and/or Chittenden common stock depending on the elections made by other Community Bank shareholders, per the allocation procedures; non-electing shareholders are subordinate (lower priority) to electing shareholders when re-allocation is required.
Shares for which no valid election is made by the election deadline are deemed "non-election shares" and are converted into the right to receive stock consideration only.

Shares for which no valid election is made are 'non-election shares' and are allocated cash or stock according to the allocation/proration procedures (used first to fill any undersubscribed form of consideration); non-electing shareholders do not get priority over electing shareholders in proration.

Non-electing shares (or shares making a 'no preference election') are treated as follows: if >50% of exchanged shares elect stock, non-electors get all cash ($23.00/share); if <50% elect stock, non-electors get stock if non-election shares are insufficient to reach the 50% stock threshold, or a combination of cash and stock if sufficient.

Shareholders/warrant holders who do not make a valid election (or make a 'no preference' election) are allocated cash, stock, or a combination thereof by the exchange agent, based on the elections made by other holders, subject to the 70%/30% stock/cash allocation and proration procedures. Dissenting shares are treated as cash election shares.

Shareholders who do not properly deliver an election (or fail to guarantee delivery) by the deadline forfeit the right to select consideration; their shares are deemed 'no election'/non-electing shares and are allocated cash and/or Chittenden common stock depending on the elections made by other shareholders, in accordance with the merger agreement's allocation provisions.

Shares for which no valid election is made ('no election shares') receive consideration in whatever form or mix remains after taking into account other stockholders' elections and proration; in practice, if cash is oversubscribed, no-election shares receive stock consideration.

Non-election shares (shares where holder made no valid election or election form not timely/properly submitted) are allocated to cash or stock based on the aggregate election results: if overall elections would push stock conversion below the 50% target, non-election shares are converted to stock first; if elections would push stock conversion above 50%, non-election shares are converted to cash first (before pro rata reallocation of cash/stock elections).

Shares for which no valid election is made, multiple elections are made, or the holder fails to follow instructions/submit certificates by the election deadline are deemed 'No Election' shares. No Election shares are subject to the allocation procedures set forth in the merger agreement and proxy statement/prospectus (i.e., holders who make no election will receive merger consideration based on the results of the allocation/proration procedures, generally implying stock unless reallocation to cash is needed to satisfy the cash pool).

Shares for which no valid election was made by the election deadline (or an invalid election was made) were deemed to have elected stock consideration (i.e., treated as 'no election shares' receiving the stock consideration, subject to adjustment).

Shares without a valid election become 'non-election' shares. They are allocated to the undersubscribed form of consideration first; if one form (cash or stock) is undersubscribed, non-election shares are allocated to that form before oversubscribed electing shares are switched. Non-election shares have lower priority than validly-elected shares in proration.

Non-electing shares are generally deemed a stock election (NCC common stock); however, if valid stock elections (including deemed non-election shares) exceed the maximum issuable shares, non-election shares may instead be converted to cash under the proration procedure.

Shares with no valid election ('non-election shares') are allocated cash and/or stock based on elections of other shareholders and the required 25%/75% cash/stock ratio, with electing shareholders getting priority in reallocation. If holders of more than 75% of shares elect stock, non-electing shareholders get cash. If less than 75% elect stock, non-electing shareholders get stock (if capacity remains) or a mix of cash and stock if needed to reach 75% stock.

Shares for which no valid election is made (or an invalid/late election) are automatically deemed to have made the Mixed Election (80% stock / 20% cash), and are allocated pro rata among non-electing holders to achieve the overall 80%/20% split.

Shares for which no valid election is made by the deadline are treated as 'non-election shares' and are converted into the right to receive cash consideration or stock consideration according to the proration methodology specified in the merger agreement (i.e., allocated to whichever consideration type is undersubscribed to help meet the Aggregate Cash/Stock Consideration targets).

If a shareholder does not make a valid election by the election deadline, the shares are designated 'non-election shares' and the exchange agent has discretion to determine the consideration type, subject to the requirement that aggregate cash consideration equals 19.5% and aggregate stock consideration equals 80.5% of total outstanding shares (non-election shares fill in whichever pool is undersubscribed).

If a CLBH shareholder does not make a valid election by the deadline (4:00 p.m. EST on [date]), First Bancorp has the authority to determine the type of consideration (cash, stock, or mix) to be exchanged for such non-election shares.

Shares with no valid election ('no election shares') are allocated cash, Wilshire stock, or a mix, depending on the aggregate cash and stock elections made by other shareholders (i.e., filled from whichever pool remains undersubscribed).

Shares for which no valid election is made (non-election shares) are allocated by the exchange agent at its discretion among cash and stock according to the allocation procedures, to help balance the aggregate 90%/10% stock/cash split.

Tendering shareholders who make no valid election receive the type of consideration (cash or stock) that is NOT oversubscribed; if neither type is oversubscribed, no-election shareholders receive cash and AMEC shares in proportion to the amounts remaining after satisfying valid elections. No-election shareholders (or those failing to specify AMEC shares vs. ADSs) who receive share consideration receive AMEC shares (not ADSs).

Shares for which no valid/timely election is made are deemed 'no election' shares; the form of consideration for such shares is determined by Farmers (or at Farmers' direction, the exchange agent) in accordance with the merger agreement's allocation/proration procedures, intended to preserve the 75% stock / 25% cash aggregate split.

Shares for which no valid election is made (or an election form is not properly completed/returned) are 'non-election shares.' These shares are used first to satisfy any shortfall needed to reach the 65% stock / 35% cash aggregate split before proration is applied to shares with an affirmative election; ultimately a non-electing holder may receive cash, stock, or a combination as determined by the allocation and proration procedures.

Shares with no valid election become 'non-election shares' and are converted to whichever form of consideration (cash or stock) is undersubscribed first, before electing shares in the oversubscribed form are subject to proration; non-election shares thus have lower priority than validly electing shares in the oversubscribed pool.

Shares for which no valid election is made are 'non-election shares' and are converted to stock or cash consideration per the allocation procedures. Non-election shares are allocated to the undersubscribed form of consideration first, ahead of electing shares in the oversubscribed form being switched/prorated.

Shareholders who make no election or an invalid election ('non-election shares') are not automatically deemed cash or stock; instead they are allocated whichever consideration type is under-subscribed as part of the proration mechanism (Section 3.4), so as to achieve the target 60% stock / 40% cash split.

If a stockholder does not submit a properly completed election form (or online election) by the election deadline, such holder is deemed to have made no election. Non-electing (or invalid election) shares are then allocated according to the proration mechanics; per the July 2020 press release, shareholders who made no election or an invalid election ultimately received 1.3 shares of Kearny common stock per MSB share (i.e., were treated as stock consideration recipients since cash was oversubscribed), plus cash in lieu of fractional shares.

Brunswick shareholders who made no election or an invalid election were deemed non-electing; non-election shares factored into the proration formula and received whichever form of consideration (cash or stock) was underelected, to bring the aggregate split to 50/50.

Shares for which no valid election is made ('non-election shares') are not automatically deemed cash or stock; instead they are allocated via the proration mechanism -- first converted to stock election shares if the cash cap is oversubscribed, or converted to cash election shares (pro rata) if the cash cap is undersubscribed, to help reach the targeted ~30% cash / 70% stock split.

Shares for which no valid election is made by the election deadline are designated 'no-election shares.' No-election shares are treated according to the allocation waterfall: if stock elections exceed the cap, no-election shares are converted to cash; if stock elections are below the cap (shortfall exists), no-election shares are first in line to be converted to stock (up to the shortfall) before cash election shares are reallocated.
Shares for which no valid election is made (non-election / 'no election shares') are deemed to have elected stock consideration.

Non-electing shares deemed to have elected the Share Option (First Merchants common stock); however, non-electing shares are the first to be converted to cash if proration requires reducing stock elections.

Shares for which no effective, properly completed election form is received by the exchange agent prior to the election deadline become 'undesignated shares.' Undesignated shares are deemed to have made an all cash election ($75.00/share) unless there is an oversubscription of the cash consideration, in which case undesignated shares are deemed to have made an all stock election (5 FNB shares/share), subject to proration.

Shareholders who fail to make a valid election (or fail to timely deliver shares/guarantee of delivery) are deemed 'non-electing' and receive merger consideration based on proration procedures: if neither cash nor stock is oversubscribed, non-electing shareholders receive cash and stock in the standard 60%/40% ratio; otherwise they receive whichever consideration remains available after electing shareholders are allocated their preferences.

Shares for which no valid election is made by the election deadline are deemed 'non-election shares.' These shares receive whatever combination of cash/stock consideration remains after satisfying the elections of stockholders who did make an election, as determined by the exchange agent to achieve the 70% stock / 30% cash allocation.

Shares for which no valid election is made ('no-election shares') are prioritized to receive the undersubscribed form of consideration (cash or stock) before oversubscribed-election shares are switched; if cash is between the min/max thresholds without proration needed, no-election shares default to stock consideration.

Shares for which no valid election was made by the election deadline are designated 'non-election shares' and are allocated stock or cash consideration according to the proration/allocation procedures (in an oversubscribed-stock scenario, non-election shares receive cash; in undersubscribed scenarios, non-election shares are first used to fill the stock shortfall).

Shareholders who fail to timely return a properly completed form of election are deemed to have made an all-cash election, subject to the same redesignation (proration) procedures as affirmative cash elections.

Shares as to which no valid election is made (or as to which the election form/letter of transmittal is not properly and timely submitted, or as to which delivery is not guaranteed by the deadline) are designated 'no election'/'non-electing' shares and are allocated cash and/or Camden common stock depending on the elections made by other Union Bankshares shareholders, subject to the merger agreement's 40%/60% allocation procedures. Non-electing shareholders are subordinate in priority to electing shareholders when reallocation is required.

NBOH shares for which no valid election is made are 'non-election shares' and are converted into cash or stock consideration per the allocation procedures; electing shares generally have priority over non-electing shares in proration (non-election shares are allocated to the undersubscribed form first).

Shares for which no valid election was made by the election deadline are 'no-election shares.' If stock is oversubscribed, no-election shares are treated as cash election shares (receive cash). If stock is undersubscribed, no-election shares are converted to stock consideration (pro rata) first to fill the shortfall before cash election shares are affected.

HVBC shareholders who do not submit a valid election (or revoke without resubmitting) are deemed 'non-election shares' and will be paid cash or stock (or a mix) in accordance with the proration procedures — i.e., if cash elections are oversubscribed, non-election shares receive stock consideration; if cash elections are undersubscribed, non-election shares receive a prorated mix including some cash.

Shares with no valid election (or multiple/invalid elections) are designated 'non-election shares.' In the shortfall scenario (cash elections <50%), non-election shares are the first pool converted to cash (pro rata) to reach the 50/50 target before touching stock-election shares; conversely if there is a cash over-election, non-election shares (along with stock-election shares) are converted to stock consideration.

Futura shareholders who fail to make a valid election (or revoke and withdraw) by the election deadline are deemed 'non-electing' and will receive all cash, all First Citizens common shares, or a combination, as determined by First Citizens or the exchange agent, allocated pro rata among non-electing holders to achieve the overall 80%/20% stock/cash ratio and satisfy elections to the greatest extent possible.

Shares with no election, late/invalid election, or revoked-and-not-resubmitted elections are treated as 'non-election shares' (also called 'no election shares'). These are allocated pro rata to fill the Stock Number first (as 'stock exchanged shares'), with any remainder converted to cash; if stock or cash elections are oversubscribed, non-election shares are simply converted to cash (in stock oversubscription) or stock (in cash oversubscription). The prospectus explicitly stated they could not predict which consideration non-election shares would receive.

Shares for which the exchange agent does not receive a properly completed cash election form (with stock certificates/book-entry delivery/guarantee of delivery) by the election deadline are exchanged for stock consideration (0.004 TD common shares plus cash in lieu of fractional shares).

Shares without a valid election ('non-election shares') are converted into cash or stock consideration per the allocation procedures in the merger agreement; non-election shares are generally allocated to the undersubscribed form of consideration before electing shareholders in the oversubscribed form are switched/prorated. Electing shareholders have priority over non-election shares if proration is necessary.

No-election shares default to stock (common stock) consideration under the disclosed oversubscription mechanics: 'each common stock election share and each no-election share shall be converted into the right to receive the per share common stock consideration.'

Shareholders who do not make a valid election (non-election shares) are paid merger consideration equivalent in value to electing holders, but may receive all cash, all stock, or a mix, depending on the remaining pool of cash and stock available after honoring valid cash and stock elections (used first to fill any cash shortfall before stock election shares).

Any First Bankshares share for which no valid cash election is made (or for which the election is revoked and not resubmitted) by the election deadline is deemed a 'non-electing share' and automatically converts into one share of the combined company (Xenith Bankshares) common stock — i.e., default is stock/retention, not cash.

Shares of holders who do not make a valid election (or fail to perfect dissenters' rights) are designated 'no-election shares.' No-election shares are converted into stock consideration as needed to fill the 80% stock pool, unless the stock consideration is oversubscribed, in which case no-election shares are converted into cash consideration instead.

If a shareholder does not submit a properly completed and signed election form by the election deadline, the shares are deemed to elect CenterState common stock (stock consideration). However, non-election shares may instead be converted to cash if the aggregate shares electing (or defaulting to) stock exceed the maximum allocable to stock consideration under the 50/50 allocation, subject to proration.

Non-election shares are treated as cash-election shares if stock is oversubscribed. If stock is undersubscribed, non-election shares are first used to absorb the stock shortfall (receiving a mix of cash and stock); only if non-election shares are insufficient to cover the shortfall do cash electors also receive a mix.

Shareholders who fail to make a valid or timely election ('non-election shares') will have the exchange agent choose the form of consideration to distribute according to allocation procedures, so that in total 70% of Carolina National shares are exchanged for stock and 30% for cash.

Shares for which no valid election was made ('non-election shares') are allocated cash and/or stock depending on the elections made by other FedFirst stockholders, and are treated together with cash election shares in the proration formula (i.e., non-election shares generally receive stock consideration unless stock is oversubscribed, in which case they receive cash along with cash electors).

Shares for which no valid election is made (non-election shares) receive merger consideration that may be cash, stock, or a combination, depending on the elections of other shareholders and the proration procedures, in order to achieve the overall 40% cash/60% stock split.

Shares with no valid election (non-election shares) are allocated stock and/or cash consideration pursuant to the merger agreement's allocation provisions, without regard to the holder's preference. In undersubscription scenarios, stock consideration is first allocated to non-election shares to fill the shortfall.

Shares for which no valid election is made (including those where holder checks 'no preference,' makes no selection, makes multiple selections, or fails to timely and properly submit the election statement/letter of transmittal) are deemed 'non-election shares.' Non-election shares receive stock and/or cash consideration as determined by ABCB in its discretion to complete the prorations necessary to achieve both the cash election maximum and stock election maximum.

Shares for which no election (or no valid election) was made prior to the election deadline (Non-Electing Shares) are automatically converted into the right to receive Stock Consideration (RCAP Class A common stock), subject to proration mechanics (i.e., treated same as Stock Election Shares).

Shares for which no valid election is made (or election form not properly returned by the deadline) are deemed 'non-election shares.' Non-election shares are first deemed cash election shares to the extent necessary to fill the 20% aggregate cash limit; if fewer non-election shares are needed, they are allocated pro rata between deemed cash and deemed stock election shares.

Shares with no valid election ('non-election shares') are first used to fill any shortfall toward the 65% stock conversion number: if the shortfall is less than or equal to non-election shares, non-election holders receive stock pro-rata for the shortfall portion and cash for the remainder; if the shortfall exceeds non-election shares, all non-election shares convert to stock. If stock is oversubscribed, non-election shares (along with cash-election shares) convert entirely to cash.

Non-election shares (no valid election made) are allocated cash or stock depending on proration outcome: if stock is oversubscribed, non-election shares (along with cash election shares) receive cash; if stock is undersubscribed (shortfall), non-election shares are first reallocated to stock to fill the shortfall before cash election shares are touched. Dissenting shares are deemed cash election shares.

Shares for which no valid election is made ('no-election shares') are allocated by the exchange agent to whichever consideration type (cash or stock) is needed to balance the 2,792,974 cash-share target after accounting for elections made by other stockholders — i.e., they absorb the shortfall/excess first before pro-rata reduction of over-elected category. Holders receiving no-election treatment could ultimately receive cash, stock, or a mix.

Shares for which no election is made (or election form not properly completed/returned) are designated "non-election shares." Non-election shares are treated flexibly depending on oversubscription/undersubscription: if stock oversubscribed, non-election shares receive cash; if stock undersubscribed, non-election shares are first used to fill any stock shortfall (receiving stock, or a mix of stock and cash) before cash election shares are affected.

Shares for which no election form is timely/properly submitted (or election is revoked without a timely replacement) are designated 'non-election shares' and are subject to the same allocation procedures as other shares (i.e., allocated cash or stock pro rata to achieve the target 55%/45% split, subject to the stock cap); election-made shares are given priority over non-election shares in the allocation. Unexercised Shore stock options are deemed to have elected cash consideration (net of exercise price).

Shareholders who do not submit a valid, properly completed and signed election form by the election deadline (or whose forms are incomplete/unsigned, or not accompanied by certificates/guaranteed delivery) are deemed non-electing. Non-electing shareholders have no control over the type of consideration received and, at Penns Woods' discretion, may receive only cash, only Penns Woods stock, or a combination, depending on the proration adjustment resulting from other shareholders' valid elections.

Shares for which no valid/effective election form was submitted by the election deadline are deemed 'no election shares.' No election shares are treated as receiving per share stock consideration unless needed as a reallocation pool to reach the 20% cash / 80% stock target, in which case a pro rata portion of no-election shares are redesignated as reallocated cash shares.

Shares for which no valid election is made are 'no-election shares.' A shareholder is deemed to have made 'no election' if they fail to follow election form/letter of transmittal instructions, if the properly completed election form and transmittal materials (or notice of guaranteed delivery) are not received by the exchange agent by the election deadline, or if a prior election is revoked without a new one being made. No-election shares are then paid in cash, stock, or a combination depending on, and after giving effect to, the valid cash and stock elections made by other shareholders (subject to proration).

Shares for which no valid election is received by the exchange agent by the election deadline are deemed 'no election shares' and are allocated cash or stock consideration according to the proration/allocation procedures (used first to fill any stock shortfall before cash election shares are converted, or converted to stock if cash is oversubscribed).

CNB stockholders who do not make a valid cash election are treated as non-election shares and will receive Bancorp common stock, subject to proration procedures (non-election shares serve as the first pool converted to cash if the minimum cash election number is not met).

Shares for which no valid election is made ('nonelection shares') are allocated cash and/or SCBT stock depending on the elections made by other TSB shareholders, and are used first (ahead of cash-election shares) to fill any shortfall in the stock allocation if total stock elections fall below 945,994 shares. Non-electing shareholders do not get priority over electing shareholders in reallocation.

Shares for which no valid election is made by the election deadline are treated as 'non-election shares' and are converted into stock and/or cash as determined by NBT according to the allocation procedures, allocated pro rata among non-electing holders to achieve the overall 65% stock / 35% cash ratio (after accounting for dissenting shares).

Shares for which a shareholder does not submit a valid, timely election (or fails to perfect dissenters' rights) are designated 'no-election shares.' The exchange agent allocates no-election shares between cash and stock consideration as needed to satisfy the aggregate cash consideration target; the shareholder may end up receiving cash, stock, or a combination depending on other shareholders' elections.

Shares for which no valid election is made ('non-electing shares') are, in all proration scenarios, first deemed to be stock election shares (i.e., default treatment is stock consideration, subject to subsequent proration).

Shares for which no valid election was made (non-election shares) are allocated according to the proration mechanics: if stock elections exceed the 621,706-share cap, non-election shares are converted 100% to cash ($31.50/share); if stock elections are under the cap, non-election shares are converted first to stock (pro rata) to help fill the 621,706-share stock cap.

Shares for which no valid cash or stock election is made by the election deadline are deemed 'non-election shares' and are allocated cash and/or stock consideration according to the proration procedures (used first to fill any stock 'shortfall' before cash-election shares are touched; if stock is oversubscribed, non-election shares are treated like cash-election shares and converted to cash).

Shares for which no valid election is made (non-election shares) receive cash, stock, or a combination thereof depending on the proration results and elections made by other shareholders; there is no fixed default to all-cash or all-stock.

Shareholders who fail to submit a valid election by the deadline (or revoke without resubmitting) are treated as 'non-electing'/'no election' shareholders; their shares are allocated cash, stock, or a combination based on the elections made by other shareholders and the proration formula, to achieve the target 75%/25% stock/cash mix.

Shares for which no valid election is made by the election deadline are deemed 'non-election shares' and are allocated cash consideration or stock consideration through the proration procedures (used first to fill any oversubscription/undersubscription of cash vs. stock elections) so that ultimately ~50% cash/~50% stock overall.

Shares for which no valid election is made ('no election shares') are treated as a distinct category and may be converted into the right to receive Peoples common shares, or, in some cases, be designated to receive cash on a pro rata basis if the exchange agent must reallocate to satisfy the cash cap.

Shares for which no valid election is made ('no election shares') are allocated cash or stock based on the overall proration outcome: if stock is oversubscribed, no election shares receive cash; if cash is oversubscribed, no election shares receive stock. Dissenting shares that lose appraisal rights are treated as no election shares.

Shares for which no valid election is made (non-election shares) are treated as 'no preference' shares; the exchange agent allocates them to cash or stock (or a combination) as needed, applying the proration formula (Section 1.5) first to non-election shares before dipping into stock-election shares, in order to achieve the ~60% stock/40% cash aggregate split.

Shares for which no valid election is submitted by the election deadline become 'undesignated shares' and are allocated first to satisfy any shortfall/excess in the required stock amount (i.e., undesignated shares may be converted to cash or stock as needed to balance the 50/50 target) before proration is applied to elected shares.

Shares with no valid election ("No Election Shares") receive cash or stock consideration as determined by the proration mechanics (generally treated similar to cash election shares unless reallocated to satisfy a stock shortfall). Restricted stock holders are deemed to have elected cash consideration to satisfy withholding obligations.

Shares as to which no election is made, or an election form is not timely submitted/perfected, or dissenter's rights are not perfected, are designated 'no election shares.' Dissenting shares are deemed cash election shares. No-election shares are then allocated to cash or stock as needed to satisfy the targeted cash consideration (30%/70% split), minimizing proration.

Shares for which no valid election is submitted by the election deadline are deemed 'No Election Shares.'
