No Election Shares are allocated by the exchange agent at its discretion (pro rata among no-election holders) to cash or stock as needed to help achieve the required 60-70% stock / 30-40% cash consideration mix, prior to any rebalancing of shares that did make an election.

If a shareholder does not make a valid or timely election, the shares are treated as 'no election shares' and are converted into cash, stock, or a mix of cash and stock consideration depending on the elections made by other Citizens shareholders (used to balance the 50/50 cash/stock allocation).

Shares with no valid election (non-election shares) are allocated at exchange agent's discretion (delegated by acquirer) to bring the aggregate consideration to exactly 30% cash / 70% stock; if elections do not already exceed caps, non-election shares are split between cash and stock as needed to reach the caps.

Shares for which no valid election form is received by the election deadline ('no election shares') are allocated cash or stock (or a combination) based on the elections made by other South Street shareholders, in accordance with the allocation/proration procedures, so that in aggregate approximately 80% of outstanding shares are exchanged for BNC stock and 20% for cash.

Shares for which no valid election is made (or election form not properly completed by the deadline) become 'non-election shares.' Under the proration formula, non-election shares are converted to cash first if the cash pool is undersubscribed; otherwise they are converted to stock consideration.

Shares for which no valid election was made (non-election shares) were allocated cash or stock depending on the aggregate elections of other shareholders and the proration formula: if stock was oversubscribed, non-election shares received cash; if stock was undersubscribed (shortfall), non-election shares were first tapped to fill the stock shortfall (pro rata) before cash election shares.

Alliance shareholders who do not return a valid election form by the election deadline (or who submit a materially defective form) are deemed to have elected stock consideration (WashingtonFirst common stock); no cash (other than cash in lieu of fractional shares).

Shares for which no valid election is made (failure to submit timely election form, revoked election not resubmitted, or failure to perfect dissenters' rights) are designated 'no-election shares.' No-election shares are subject to the allocation procedure: they are first deemed cash election shares to the extent needed to satisfy the minimum cash consideration target; any remaining no-election shares are treated as stock election shares (i.e., receive PPBI stock).

Shares for which no valid election form is timely submitted are deemed 'non-election shares' and are allocated cash or stock consideration (or split) pursuant to the proration formula in the merger agreement, not a fixed default.

Shares for which no valid election is made (no election checked, improperly completed, certificates not submitted, or election revoked without timely resubmission) are deemed 'non-election shares.' Non-electing holders will receive all cash, all S&T stock, or a mix, as determined under the merger agreement's allocation/proration procedures (at S&T's discretion), and shares with an affirmative election have priority over non-election shares if reallocation is necessary.

Shares for which no valid election is made (non-election shares, including those without properly completed election forms/certificates or guarantee of delivery by the deadline) are allocated cash, stock, or a combination depending on the elections made by other stockholders, in order to achieve the overall 80% stock / 20% cash split; if stock is oversubscribed, non-election shares receive cash.

Shares for which no valid election is made by the deadline are 'non-election shares' and are allocated by Chemung Financial on a pro rata basis among non-electing holders to achieve the overall 75% stock / 25% cash ratio (after accounting for dissenting shares).

Shares for which no valid election is made (or election form not timely submitted/revoked without cure) are treated as 'non-election shares.' Non-election shares are allocated per the proration formula: if neither cash nor stock is oversubscribed, non-election shares are first allocated to stock (up to filling the Stock Number) on a pro rata basis, with the remainder converted to cash. If stock is oversubscribed, non-election shares receive cash; if cash is oversubscribed, non-election shares receive stock.

Shares with no valid election are deemed to have elected stock consideration; however, if the IES common stock value (VWAP) is less than $4.024, non-election shares are instead deemed to have elected cash consideration (subject to the maximum cash amount).

Shares whose holders do not make a valid/timely election (no-election shares) or who fail to properly submit an election form by the deadline are deemed to have elected Old Line Bancshares common stock (stock election), subject to the 95%/5% allocation and proration rules.

Shareholders who do not submit a valid election (or revoke without resubmitting) by the election deadline are deemed 'non-electing'/'no election' shareholders and receive Village Bank and Trust Financial Corp. common stock for 80% of their RCB shares and cash for the remaining 20% of their RCB shares (i.e., treated as a mixed/combination election), subject to further re-allocation only if needed to satisfy the 80/20 aggregate requirement.

Shares for which no valid election is submitted (or an election is revoked without resubmission) by the election deadline are deemed 'no election shares,' which are subject to the merger agreement's allocation/proration provisions (may be designated cash or stock on a pro rata basis as needed to satisfy the 40-60% cash/stock bands). Dissenting shareholders' shares are deemed cash election shares for reallocation purposes.

Shares for which no valid election is made become 'undesignated shares.' If stock elections exceed the Stock Amount cap (oversubscribed for stock), undesignated shares are deemed cash elections. If stock elections are under the cap, undesignated shares are allocated pro rata toward the Stock Amount (i.e., treated preferentially as stock, up to the cap). Holders are told they may receive stock, cash, or a combination depending on other shareholders' elections.

Stockholders who fail to make a valid election by the election deadline are deemed to have elected to receive cash and stock consideration in amounts depending on the amount of cash and stock consideration remaining available after other stockholders' elections (i.e., default/non-election shares are allocated the residual mix after prorating elected shares).

For non-election shares, Parent (First National) has authority (delegable to exchange agent) to determine consideration type; ultimately non-election shares are allocated as needed to fill the aggregate cash/stock limits (typically default to stock consideration if cash limit already filled, or cash if stock limit filled).

Shares for which no valid election is made ('non-election shares') are converted into cash or stock consideration according to the allocation procedures; specifically, non-election shares are the first source drawn upon to fill an undersubscribed cash pool (converted to cash consideration) before stock-election shares are converted.

Non-electing shares: allocated (1) stock if cash election is oversubscribed, (2) cash if stock election is oversubscribed, (3) stock if neither is oversubscribed until the stock maximum is reached, after which remaining non-electing shares are deemed tendered for cash. Holders who fail to submit a valid letter of election and transmittal within 30 days after such letters are sent are deemed to have made no election.

Shares for which no valid election is made by the deadline become 'non-election shares' and are first in line to be converted to cash consideration (if cash pool is undersubscribed) or otherwise allocated per the allocation procedures; effectively non-election shares are treated preferentially for cash conversion ahead of stock-election shares when cash is undersubscribed.

Shares for which no valid election is made by the election deadline are deemed 'non-election shares' and are convertible at Mid Penn's discretion into cash, stock, or a combination, subject to the proration/allocation procedures designed to meet the 80%/20% stock/cash split.

Shares with no valid election by the election deadline are 'non-electing shares.' If aggregate cash elections (excluding non-electing shares) are between 15% and 25% of outstanding shares, non-electing shares default to STOCK consideration. If aggregate cash elections exceed 25% (max cash), non-electing shares are also converted to STOCK. If aggregate cash elections are below 15% (min cash), non-electing shares are converted to CASH first (pro-rata) to help reach the 15% minimum, and only afterward, if still below minimum, remaining shares are prorated per formula.

Shares for which no valid election is submitted by the election deadline are deemed 'mixed election shares' and receive the per share mixed consideration (0.60 shares × exchange ratio + $6.60 cash), subject to the same allocation/proration procedures as other shares.

Shares with no valid election become 'no election shares' and are allocated to whichever form of consideration (cash or stock) is undersubscribed, before switching properly-electing shares of the oversubscribed form; electing shares have priority over no-election shares in any needed proration.

Shares for which no valid election form is timely received (or a revoked election with no replacement) are deemed 'non-election shares.' These are not automatically cash or stock; they are subject to the allocation procedures and are given lower priority than validly-elected shares (elections receive priority in allocation over non-election shares). The ultimate treatment of non-election shares depends on whether cash/stock elections exceed their respective caps.

Shares with no valid election (non-election shares) are allocated per the proration formula—generally treated like cash-election shares when stock is oversubscribed (all converted to cash), or used to fill any stock shortfall (pro-rated to stock) when stock is undersubscribed. In the actual outcome, non-electing shareholders received all-stock (1.1743 shares per CKF share), same as stock electors, since stock was not oversubscribed.

Shares for which no valid election is made (or election is not timely/properly submitted) are designated 'no-election shares' and are converted into cash or stock (or a mix) depending on the elections of other stockholders and the allocation/proration procedures, in order to achieve the target cash conversion number.
Shares for which no valid cash or stock election is made (non-election shares) are deemed to elect and receive stock consideration.

Shares of shareholders who make no election (or check the non-election box) receive a presumptive 50% cash / 50% LCNB stock allocation, subject to the overall allocation procedures (i.e., non-electing shares are also used to fill the cash pool to reach the 50% aggregate cash requirement if needed).
Citizens shareholders who did not submit a properly completed election form prior to the election deadline would receive Riverview stock (i.e., default treatment is stock consideration).

Shares for which no valid election is submitted (or election is revoked and not resubmitted) by the election deadline are designated 'non-election shares.' Non-election shares are treated as cash-election shares if the stock election is oversubscribed; if undersubscribed, non-election shares may receive some stock consideration on a pro-rata basis per the shortfall formula.

Shares with no valid election (no box checked, multiple boxes checked, or election form/certificates not timely received) are deemed 'non-electing' / 'no election shares'. Non-electing shares are allocated cash, stock, or a combination by NB&T/exchange agent to achieve the overall 50% cash / 50% stock ratio, satisfying other shareholders' elections to the greatest extent possible subject to that ratio.

Shares of Regal Bancorp common stock for which no valid election is made ('no-election shares') are automatically converted into the right to receive Old Line Bancshares common stock (the stock consideration), not cash.
GNB shareholders who make no election or an invalid election are deemed non-electing and will receive LINK common stock (stock consideration) as default.

Shares for which no valid election is made (or an improperly completed/late election form) are designated 'non-election shares' and are allocated cash and/or Orrstown stock depending on the elections made by other stockholders, in order to achieve the 85%/15% stock/cash target; electing stockholders are given priority over non-electing stockholders in any required re-allocation.

Shares for which no valid election is made (no election, improperly completed, untimely, or revoked election) are deemed 'non-election shares.' If cash election is oversubscribed, non-election shares receive stock consideration. If cash election is undersubscribed, non-election shares are first in line (before stock-election shares) to be converted to cash to fill the shortfall, prorated if necessary.

Shares with no valid election (non-election / no-election shares) are deemed to have made no election and will receive whatever consideration (cash, stock, or mix) is necessary to satisfy the 60%/40% proration and allocation provisions of the merger agreement; no-election shares are used first (before cash-election shares) to fill any stock undersubscription.

Shares for which no valid election is made (or election form not returned properly completed) by the election deadline are treated as 'non-election shares' and are converted into stock consideration or cash consideration as necessary to achieve the 75% stock / 25% cash allocation (used first to fill any stock shortfall before cash election shares are converted).

Shares for which no valid election is made (including failure to submit form, revocation without resubmission, or checking 'no election' box) are deemed 'no election shares' and are subject to allocation/proration procedures; no-election shares receive lower priority than validly-elected shares in the allocation.

Akron shareholders who make no election (or an invalid election) are deemed non-electing and are treated as having made a Stock Election; they receive CNB common stock (Stock Consideration), subject to overall proration mechanics (non-election shares are never converted to cash under the proration formula).

Shares for which no valid election is made (non-election shares) are allocated per formula: if cash elections are oversubscribed (>30%), non-election shares receive stock consideration entirely; if cash elections are undersubscribed (<30%), non-election shares are allocated a prorated mix of cash (to fill remaining cash pool up to 30% cap) and stock, using a fraction based on the shortfall percentage.

Shares with no valid, timely election became 'undesignated shares.' Undesignated shares were used by the exchange agent (via random lot selection) to fill any shortfall needed to reach the Aggregate Company Share Amount (stock) or otherwise; if all undesignated shares are allocated to one side and a shortfall/excess still remains, the proration factor mechanism is applied. If exactly at target, undesignated shares are converted to cash consideration by default.

Bank of Richmond shareholders who do not submit a properly completed election form (or revoke it) by the election deadline are designated 'non-election shares.' Non-electing shares are allocated to cash or stock (or both) as needed to satisfy the 50% cash/50% stock aggregate requirement, per the proration mechanics (treated first as stock if cash election number=50%, or filling shortfalls in cash or stock as applicable).

Shares as to which no valid cash or stock election is made (or election is deemed invalid/revoked, including failure to timely deliver certificates under a guarantee of delivery) are 'non-election shares' and receive stock and/or cash consideration as determined by the proration formula (Section 2.5(b)) — i.e., non-election shares are treated as a residual pool allocated to balance the 42% cash cap, not automatically defaulted to cash or stock.

Shares for which no valid election is made (or election form not timely/properly submitted) become 'no election shares.' No election shares are allocated cash, stock, or a combination depending on the elections made by other shareholders (per the proration formula), not a fixed default.

Shares of Island common stock for which no valid election was made (or an election form not properly completed/returned) were deemed 'non-election shares'; the consideration received by non-electing/non-election shareholders would depend on the elections made by other shareholders and the allocation/proration procedures (i.e., non-election shares are allocated cash and/or stock as needed to achieve the 80%/20% stock/cash split).

Shares of a non-electing holder default to a mix: the holder is deemed to have elected cash consideration for a percentage of shares equal to (aggregate cash consideration) / (closing SWK NAV), with the remainder of shares defaulting to the per share stock consideration. Effectively, non-election shares default toward stock consideration for the balance beyond the deemed-cash percentage, subject to the same proration if aggregate elections exceed caps.

Shares for which no valid election is made (or an invalid/late election) are deemed 'non-election shares.' Non-election shares are allocated cash and/or stock consideration as needed to balance the 50%/50% cash-stock split; if stock is oversubscribed, non-election shares receive cash; if cash is oversubscribed, non-election shares receive stock; if neither is oversubscribed, non-election shares are split to make the aggregate cash and stock totals equal the Cash/Stock Conversion Numbers.

Shares for which no valid election is made (non-election shares) are deemed to receive 'mixed consideration' — i.e., 75% converted to stock consideration and 25% to cash consideration (subject to cash in lieu of fractional shares).
